messages:
sara: Heads-up - we started seeing 99th pct nvme latency spikes on preemptible GPU nodes in us-west-2 around 09:05 UTC. Affected pods are mostly batch-inference workers. :eyes:
infra-bot: ALERT: node gpu-preempt-08 nvme.io_wait=482ms, queue_depth=64 (threshold=100ms) — tags: us-west-2, preemptible
matt: on it. initial glance: ephemeral cleaner jobs ran at 09:03 across many nodes, maybe overlapping with heavy batching?
jia: can you paste the iostat/fio for the node? I suspect small-random reads at high concurrency.
sara: log snippet from gpu-preempt-08 right after spike:
```
[09:05:13] fio: write: IOPS=12k, BW=120MiB/s, lat (usec)= 1200/8000/20000
[09:05:14] nvme0n1: submission queue full, q_depth=64, inflight=60
kernel: blk-mq: dispatch stuck for 1200 ms
```
matt: that looks like queue depth saturation not sustained write wear. Preemptible nodes have a lower NVMe queue_depth tunable in our AMI for safety (64). Batch jobs expect 512.
jia: yep, config mismatch. Scheduler put high-concurrency batches on these nodes because they had available GPU capacity. We should add a placement constraint or adjust queue_depth only on dedicated nodes.
sara: immediate mitigation: matt, can you cordon preemptible pool and drain current batch pods to dedicated pool? fallback to slower concurrency.
matt: started drain script now: `kubectl drain gpu-preempt-08 --ignore-daemonsets --force` — will route new batch jobs away.
leo: filed INF-4223 to track root cause + long-term: adapt scheduler to avoid high-iops workloads on low-qdepth nves and add probe that compares AMI nvme settings vs cluster baseline.
jia: long-term: consider dynamic queue_depth via systemd hook or setting io_uring params per workload. Also add a preflight check in batch job admission that runs fio microprobe to estimate expected qd.
sara: cost note: preemptible pool saves ~40% on GPU EC2 cost but we can't let it blow latency SLAs. Add to ticket: cost vs tail-latency SLO tradeoff analysis.
infra-bot: NOTE: autoscaler will still attempt to use preemptible nodes for best-effort jobs. We should add labelling: `workload.io_sensitivity=low` to allow autoscaler optimization.
matt: post-drain metrics trending back to normal 09:09 UTC. nvme lat 99th -> 45ms. keeping cordoned while we iterate. :white_check_mark:
